label: Analysis settings of the v4 study (hri_analysis_v4.py): intervals, the archived v3 results used for research question 1, and the differences between v3 and v4 that are listed under the comparison table. Reporting only.
declared: 2026-10-24, before any v4 recording exists. Frozen with the other v4 configs.

bootstrap.why: Frames, asks and junctions within one run are not independent (the same worker, the same view), so the intervals for gesture accuracy, coverage, angle error and time resample whole RUNS with replacement (cluster bootstrap), not frames. Wilson intervals on frame counts are also given, labelled as frame-level. 2000 resamples and seed 1 are fixed here so the intervals are reproducible; they are not tuned.

avatar_experiment.declared: 2026-11-21, Anisha (AUDIT.md 16.31.1, review of the same day), before any recording and before the reporting step exists. Reporting only.
avatar_experiment.bootstrap: the numbers of the block 'bootstrap' above (n_resamples 2000, seed 1, percentiles 2.5 and 97.5), resampling TAKES with replacement within each look x command x distance x arm cell; a pooled cell resamples the takes of each of its looks separately (the look composition stays fixed)
avatar_experiment.frame_measures: computed as a share per take (a single frame is 0 or 1), reported as the mean over takes with the bootstrap over takes
avatar_experiment.wilson: only for take-level yes/no outcomes (a sequence read as recorded / as another command / not read; single-frame takes counted on their own), with wilson_z above; never over frames

floor.per: arm and distance (valid takes of a look x command cell)

avatar_experiment.why: The frames of one take (11 of a held pose, 21 of a swing) are one performance seen many times: they are not independent, so a frame is never a unit of an interval. Frames, asks and junctions of the navigation runs are handled the same way with the unit 'run' (block 'bootstrap').

rq1_note: Research question 1: can the robot understand natural, moving gestures as reliably as v3's fixed poses? The table compares the v3 Task 2 route (original final and replication) and the v3 Task 1 final with each v4 setting on the measures both can compute. Success and the junction reads are the comparable core; times depend on the machine and are marked.
declared_differences: Gestures: v3 shows fixed arm poses (LEFT / RIGHT arm out, FORWARD arm up or fist, STOP open palm); v4 shows natural, moving POINT (any angle), WAIT (index finger up) and STOP, with varying speed, size, arm and start delay.

Reader: v3 classifies the arm angle of one frame into five fixed directions (three kept) plus MediaPipe STOP; v4 reads a 1.0 s window (gesture_motion.py: moving gesture, held pose, hand landmarks) and returns an angle.

STOP and WAIT: v3 STOP was MediaPipe's Open_Palm label at score 0.5 or more (configs/hri_perception.json stop.min_confidence); v4 reads STOP from the open-palm finger geometry (four fingers extended and spread) and WAIT from the index-up geometry, and does NOT require MediaPipe's label or its score: they are logged per frame and reported only (decided 2026-11-08, AUDIT.md 14.16). Reason: in the look check MediaPipe said Open_Palm in 5 per cent of STOP frames although the geometry passed in 66 to 97 per cent. A false STOP is safe, a missed STOP is not. Extended 2026-11-16 (AUDIT.md 16.18.2, decided after the STOP-session results, development only, before the freeze): the v4 STOP also needs the fingertips spread (distance index tip to pinky tip over distance index knuckle to pinky knuckle at least 1.3) and a RAISED arm (the reader's own arm-raised flag), so that the flat PROCEED hand and a hanging open hand no longer read STOP (gesture_motion.stop_extra_ok; hand.stop_requires_raised and hand.stop_fingertip_spread_min in configs/v4/gesture_reader.json); there is no stillness cue (it read true STOPs late). This reverses the part of the decision of 2026-11-08 that STOP needs no arm keypoints. Cost and limitation: 21 of 39 true STOPs in the STOP sessions are read later than with the earlier reader (median +0.21 s, at most +0.60 s), none is lost, and the PROCEED hand still gives some false STOPs (66 frames, 28 episodes over every PROCEED frame of the sessions against 535 and 56 with the earlier reader). Extended 2026-11-17 (AUDIT.md 16.19.7, C2s, chosen AFTER seeing the replay of 16.19.6 and disclosed there, development only, before the freeze): while the robot is stopped (below 0.05 m/s, in the states read and approach) a v4 STOP also needs the hand still over the 0.3 s stop window (the wrist speed at most the reader's still_speed_max); while the robot moves the STOP rule is exactly as before (gesture_reader.json hand.stop_still_when_robot_stopped, control.json stop_rule). Criterion (a) of 16.18.2 is NOT met: of the 40 true STOPs of the STOP sessions 32 are read within 1.0 s instead of 34 (two are read later, +0.20 s and +0.90 s), 25 STOPs are read about 0.2 s later (median +0.21 s), no STOP the earlier reader reads is lost, and the readings while the robot moves are identical to the earlier reader on the replay data. Benefit: the false STOPs in the step-5 logs fall from 216 frames and 150 episodes to 73 and 65. No split of criterion (a) by the robot state at the first reading was computed, to avoid trying definitions after seeing results.

Decision: v3 maps a direction class to a branch; v4 resolves a pointed angle to a branch with the roadmap (the arrival branch is never valid, within 30 deg), with a second look from a sideways shift and a re-approach of the commander when needed.

Dialog hold: v4 accepts a reading held 0.5 s (control.json dialog.gesture_hold_s); v3 held 1.0 s (hri_control.json, frozen). Re-ask shift: v4 moves 0.8 m to the side before looking again (control.json dialog.reask_shift_m, initial, chosen from the simulator two-view study); v3 moved 0.4 m (frozen). All other dialog timings (approach distance 2.0 m, ask window 5 s, two asks) are the v3 values.
Several people: v4 scenes may have bystanders, one of whom commands (commander rule: facing the robot, hand moving, gesture started after the question); v3 had one worker per stop and no bystanders.
Zoom: v4 can narrow the pan-tilt field of view onto the hand (zoom on / off settings); v3 used a fixed 60 deg view.
Avatar looks: v4 uses several looks and clips, split into development and test (the test look and clips were never used in development); v3 used one Mixamo worker.
Protocol and scene: v4 speaks protocol 3 (HUD, zoom, truth files) in the v4 scene; v3 spoke protocol 2 in the v3 scene.
Truth: v4 scores against per-frame truth (truth.jsonl) and the optimal path on a grid; v3 scored against the command shown at each junction.

Runs and seeds: the number of runs per setting, the seed and the machine are those of configs/v4/final_plan.json and the session records; v3 used 10 runs per task, seed 2. Inference times, stale-perception stops and total times depend on the machine and are not comparable across machines.

PROCEED valid frames (v4 only, AUDIT.md 16.21, adopted 2026-11-17 before Nusrat's strict-protocol rerun): the reader reads PROCEED (the forearm swing, a v4 gesture; v3 has none) when the arm is valid in at least max(10, 0.6 x the frames it received for the person in the 2.0 s window) frames (configs/v4/gesture_reader.json proceed.min_valid_floor); the earlier v4 rule was 0.6 x the nominal 20 = 12. At the nominal 10 Hz the two are the same; at a lower frame rate the rule follows what arrived. In the replay of 16.19.6 no STOP reading changed and the step-5 PROCEED holds rose from 35/62 to 58/62 (59/62 with C2s).

Checkpoint workers (variants T3 and T4, simulator; AUDIT.md 16.23 to 16.26.9): TESTED AND NOT ADOPTED. The finals run without checkpoint workers (control files lie_detection.checkpoint false and next_junction_back false; the guard refuses any checkpoint key on); v3 has none. What was tested: one worker beside each branch leaving a decision junction (later seven fixed positions) shows PROCEED toward the goal or points back on a wrong branch (a liar shows the opposite), and a 'back' sends the robot back to the junction (T3 always; T4 only when the junction's answers disagreed, plus a BACK vote at the next junction). T3 was not adopted (16.23.1: 6 lies caught and 6 false backtracks per row, net about zero). T4 was designed after seeing T3 and adopted on 2026-11-18 (16.24.3) on an out-of-sample gain of +20.0 pp in B3 on and B4 on (corrected to +17.5 pp in 16.25.0; Newcombe 95% -3.2 to +36.2, which touched zero) in a simulator that read every pointing. It was dropped on 2026-11-20 by the stopping rule declared before the final check (16.26.8, 16.26.9): its in-sample gains did not survive the readability model of 16.26.6 (the probability that a pointing is read depends on its angle to the line of sight, fitted on the development data; pessimistic by design); on fresh simulator seeds 101 to 140 (40 runs per row, 900 s, side view off, the model in both T0 and T4) the gain is +0.0 pp in B3 on (24/40 against 24/40) and +0.0 pp in B4 on (23/40 against 23/40), no A row changed. For information: the same settings on seeds 21 to 60 gave +5.0 pp and +7.5 pp; a first rerun with the side view on (16.26.7) was contaminated by a stall of the side view and is not evidence. LIMITATION: with two workers per node and consistent liars, a lie toward a valid branch is not detectable from the available evidence; in the simulator a first-asked consistent liar fooled the robot 19 times and the second opinion caught a lie only twice (16.21.3), and turning backtrack on added 1/20 because a lie toward a valid branch is never rejected (16.22). Simulator results only: nothing was run in Unity.
